<summary>
Turn 1 attempted to list images with a malformed “ls -ალ …” (non-ASCII option) and got “ls: invalid option”. Turn 2 successfully listed /app/workspace/dataset/img showing multiple .jpg files (e.g., 007.jpg … 097.jpg). Turn 3 counted 22 image files.

Turn 4 tried running OCR with “python” but python was not found. Turn 5 reran with python3 and successfully OCR’d 007.jpg, showing an invoice with “GRAND TOTAL : 20.00” and a timestamp line “23-01-2019 …”. Turn 6 verified openpyxl is installed (3.1.5).

Turn 7 ran a first full OCR+parsing script across all images using multiple preprocessing variants and tesseract configs, extracting date and total. Output (completed across Turns 7–10) produced dates/totals for all 22 files but had issues: 019.jpg total extracted as 0.00, 069.jpg total None, 071.jpg date None, and some totals likely wrong.

Turn 11 inspected best OCR text for 019.jpg, 069.jpg, and 071.jpg. Findings:
- 019.jpg includes “Total Ri = 86. 00” and “Total Gross ARM 86.00” plus date “18/03/18 …”.
- 069.jpg includes “Total Sales (Inclusive GST) RM 9.90” and date “20-02-18”.
- 071.jpg includes “Sub-total 17.76”, “Total Sales Incl GST 17.76”, “Total After Adj [nce] GST 17.70”, and date “19/62/2018 …” (OCR noise), plus invoice number containing “20180219…”.

Turn 12 debugged why 019.jpg became 0.00: the amount regex found “86” and “00” separately from “86. 00” and the code picked the last token (“00”), cleaning to 0.00.

Turn 13 introduced an improved extraction approach:
- More robust amount token regex to capture spaced decimals (e.g., “86. 00”) and comma decimals (e.g., “50,76”).
- Scoring of candidate lines (GRAND TOTAL highest, then TOTAL AFTER, TOTAL DUE, NET TOTAL, TOTAL SALES, TOTAL GROSS, TOTAL/AMOUNT) plus exclusions for SUBTOTAL, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED; also skips “GST SUMMARY/TAX SUMMARY” sections and avoids plain CASH payment lines.
- Date extraction improved by adding an “invoice_ymd_re” to parse dates embedded in long invoice numbers (e.g., 20180219…).

The improved run’s output streamed in Turns 13–15 (not yet complete by Turn 15) and showed corrected/changed results for many files, including:
007 2019-01-23 20.00; 009 2018-01-18 11.00; 010 2017-12-29 14.10; 011 2017-06-15 15.00; 019 2018-03-18 86.00; 034 2018-08-09 332.30; 039 2018-03-30 189.75; 052 2018-03-23 10.00; 063 2018-02-26 85.54; 064 2018-02-21 1.00; 069 2018-02-20 9.90; 071 2018-02-19 17.70; 074 2018-03-20 102.00; 077 2017-10-29 21.30; 078 2017-02-02 80.00; 080 2017-09-21 10.40; 083 2017-05-30 18.80; 087 2017-07-27 538.00; 088 2017-08-09 99.80.
The remaining files (090/094/097) were not yet printed by the end of this window, so the improved parsing process was still running/streaming output.
</summary>
